newsitem.title: FRANCE: New British foreign secretary to visit Paris, Bonn.
newsitem.headline: New British foreign secretary to visit Paris, Bonn.

text.p: New British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook will make his first foreign trip since taking office to Paris on Wednesday, meeting France's foreign minister and its Socialist opposition leader, French officials said on Tuesday.

Cook, appointed last Friday after the Labour party's landslide general election victory on Thursday, is due to travel on the same day to Bonn for talks with Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, the German foreign ministry announced.
In Paris, he will meet his French counterpart, Herve de Charette, over lunch to discuss European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation issues, a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

"We have noted statements by Mr Cook indicating that Britain wants to promote a constructive engagement in the European Union," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told Reuters. "We are happy to welcome him to Paris in that spirit."

Before seeing de Charette, Cook will go to Socialist party headquarters to meet French opposition leader Lionel Jospin, who is campaigning to oust the centre-right government in snap parliamentary elections called for May 25 and June 1.

The French left has taken heart from British Prime Minister Tony Blair's triumph, saying it showed Europe was moving to the left, while the ruling conservative coalition has argued that Blair's New Labour party had only won by abandoning old-style socialism in favour of free-market policies.

Doutriaux said the main topics for the foreign ministers' talks would be the EU's impending reform summit, the British six-month presidency of the EU next year when countries joining a single European currency will be selected, building the Western European Union defence grouping and reforming NATO.
Britain's European Affairs Minister Doug Henderson visited Brussels on Monday and promised a "fresh start" after years of antagonism from the former ruling Conservatives.
Henderson will also accompany Cook on Wednesday, the British embassy in Bonn said in a statement.

"Cook's aim is to make contact with his colleagues in the key European capitals as quickly as possible. His visit indicates the intention of the British government to make a new start in its relations within Europe," the statement said.

"Europe, for the new British government, is an opportunity, not a threat," Henderson said on Monday. He said Britain would sign the EU's Social Chapter on workers' rights, agree to more qualified majority voting in some policy areas and support a new employment chapter in a new EU treaty.
Cook will also meet Oskar Lafontaine, the leader of Labour's German sister party, the Social Democrats (SPD), in Bonn.

Blair's landslide election victory has plunged the SPD into a period of soul-searching, as they try to find parallels they hope will help them return to power after 16 years in opposition in general elections due in late 1998.
